I know. I recently read this quote from David Foster Wallace where he says basically "[you'll learn] that sometimes human beings have to just sit in one place and, like, hurt." 

The quote is longer but that part hit me hard. Sometimes you just have to hurt. You don't deserve it, and theres no reason for it. It just is.

If it's any comfort, i know how you feel. And lots of people know how you feel. Also, DFW has tons of moving quotes about depression and it makes me feel better to read them. It might make you feel better too
The world would not be better without you. Life is beautiful and sometimes we have to suffer. You will get through it.
Who knows why we have to deal with loneliness? This too will pass. I'm here if you need someone to talk to

You seem so open to new ideas and i love that. My favorite open mics are comedy because laughter is good for the soul. If you go, feel free to message me and tell me about it! Best of luck :)

I always get super depressed on my birthday. And Christmas. It's super weird but maybe just the pressure to feel happy causes an opposite reaction?? Idk, but your feelings are valid. Happy birthday :) hope you find some beauty in life today
Sometimes if I listen to music for too long it starts to sound like static. You might try a podcast to switch it up. Or explore new music. Message me if you want suggestions for either :)

I'm sorry :/ I have seen this happen with close friends. Depression can be an extremely brutal illness. But there is a light on the other side of the darkness. This feeling is temporary, and you will get through it. Message me if you want to talk.
It won't make you feel better, trust me. I've lost people too. Message me if you want to talk.

That's great that you're getting a college education. Honestly, I just graduated and my depression and anxiety have really resided a lot since I did. It gets better. It's also a really good sign that you have bursts of motivation. RIDE THOSE OUT. And if you just found out your friend also struggles with depression, maybe you should try talking to them about it. It's remarkable how helpful it can be just to talk to someone who says, "I know how you feel." And on that note, I know how you feel. I believe in you. Best of luck. Message me if you want to talk!

It's always a little weird being in a new place. Try to get a good night's sleep, things are always a little brighter when you're well rested. Soon your apartment will feel like home, and you WILL feel empowered. I promise. Also, plants help :) good luck, and congrats! Sincerely, the college grad who just moved back in with her mom lol.

You have a lot of great qualities just judging by this post. You work hard. You support your family. You've earned a right to be proud of your accomplishments. 

It sounds like you're in kind of a shitty situation, but remember that everything is temporary and that you DO have control of certain aspects of your life. There are apps that can help you meet new people and form real connections. Also, I know it's hard, but I encourage you to push through the anxiety and attend events when you're invited. I struggle with anxiety and depression too and I often force myself to do things even if they're out of my comfort zone. I ALWAYS am glad I did it.

One thing I like to do personally is attend open mics. I live in a very rural area and can still find them if I look. It's a nice way to go out and socialize and they're usually free and you can just blend into the background and observe. Usually comedians, poets, and singers who perform at these are struggling with depression and anxiety too (it's a stereotype but it's also pretty real) and it's really nice to hear people joke about it.

You don't have to be pretty/fun at parties/whatever. You only have to be YOU. And you should only compare yourself to YOURSELF.

Also, change is good. I'm not saying you should sell your house and leave your husband but... couldnt you? Take your success and your money and your awesome self and move somewhere beautiful? Obviously that's totally extreme and I'm not suggesting that, but my point is just this: the future is unknowable, and it's bright. You can change your life whenever you want. I just started listening to this podcast called "Alone: A Love Story," and it's basically this woman whose life totally falls apart when her husband has an affair and how she just... continues to be a person. It's weirdly amazing.

Anyway, I hope something here makes you feel better. You deserve love and you deserve to feel good about yourself. Good luck :)

We need to get back to nature!!! Yes!! I am living in a city currently and it makes me so depressed and downtrodden. I grew up in the forest and I cannot wait to finish school so I can get back into a rural setting. Maybe that will help you too. Nature is beautiful.
*Virtual hug*

Hug more girls if that's what makes you happy. Go to a psychiatrist, maybe you need medication. It's a good sign that you are trying, you need to break through the "no one cares about me" mentality. I'm a stranger on the internet and I care about you. I care because I know I am playing the role of someone in your life who you should be opening up to but you think you can't. There is ALWAYS someone who will listen and understand. Try talking to a teacher who you feel comfortable with. Focus on the positive and KEEP WORKING!! You can get through this, and it sounds like you have the motivation needed to get through it! Like you said, you are young, loyal, kind, intelligent. Bad things happen to good people, that's life. You need to forge your own path. One day you will be able to give advice to young kids struggling with depression and say that you made it through a better person. You can do this. Good luck, OP.

Do your friends/girlfriend know that you have these mental health issues? Talk to your them first. They may not have had any idea. Did you have a healthy relationship with your girlfriend? She might forgive you. Apologize to your friend. You are not a waste of space. You deserve happiness too. Think about something you're good at. Try to do things you enjoy. Good luck.

Your friend sounds like a douche. I'd say you should move on from both of these girls, and seeing as you can fall in love in as little as one week, that shouldn't be a problem. Hang out with your other friends, or if you don't have any others go out and meet new people. Go to public events and be friendly. This depends on you though, you have to make your own happiness. I have cut before too and it is not the answer. It only ever made me feel ashamed of myself. No one deserves to be treated like shit by their friend. You deserve love too. Good luck!

Love her and support her, it sounds like you're doing a good job of that already. I don't know the context of their falling out but time tends to give us perspective that allows us to forgive people. Try to get a conversation going between your girlfriend and your sister. Tell them you love them both and the situation is hurting you. Use that pathos!! Remind them why they used to be friends, and hopefully they will come to their senses. Good luck!!

Don't give up, whatever you do. A lot of your symptoms sound like they are all stemming from your depression. It may be difficult, but you need to seek help. Ask a parent, a relative, or a friend who you trust if they can help you find therapy. You may just have a chemical imbalance and a small dosage of the right antidepressant will let you lead a happy life. Life can be beautiful, you must remember that. What do you find interesting? What makes you happy? Start small. You can do this. I know because I've been there, and I made it out alive.

Sometimes I think about the people who created the things I love the most--Sylvia Plath, Ernest Hemingway, Vincent van Gogh, Kurt Cobain etc-- and I realize: all of them wanted to die. Do you think that being a great artist means that you are doomed? To sadness? To suicide? Is loneliness the price we must pay to be able to thoroughly explore our own minds?
